title: Mayan City-States
capsule: The Maya city-states of this earlier era emerged during the Preclassic and into the Classic period, spanning roughly 247 BC to 850 CE across the lowlands of southern Mexico, Guatemala, and Belize. Rather than a single polity, this was a mosaic of independent, dynastic city-states — including Tikal, Calakmul, Palenque, and Copán — sharing a common script, calendar, and religious culture while remaining politically autonomous and often at war with one another. The period ended with the still-debated Classic Maya collapse of the 8th–9th centuries, when the great southern lowland centers were abandoned, giving way to a successor constellation of Postclassic city-states farther north.

citations.label: The collapse of Classic Maya civilization - Britannica

attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Major Classic-period city locations and rough territorial spheres of influence are reconstructed from LiDAR survey, excavation, and epigraphy; outer boundaries between polities and the full extent of any given city-state's control are interpreted from limited epigraphic and archaeological evidence, making the geometry a broad approximation. Capsule researched for this polity/era specifically (confidence: medium).
